dispositions.rationale: The registry is a chain (ACE-D9); the current template must be its last entry, and every entry after the first needs a reproducible improves report against the one before it, so no digest becomes a baseline without a comparison.
A calibration record names the judge model ID it calibrated; a mismatch with the run refuses the task.
ACE-A42 now covers C18 alone; C19 to C27 and C29 each have a criterion, ACE-A57 to ACE-A66.

The file names in the slice list are where each slice puts its behaviour, not promised deliverables; the obligations are the behaviours the criteria check, and an artifact criterion on a filename is what the observable-obligation rule warns against.
The installer suite already holds test_eval_corpora_never_deploy_for_any_tool, which stages every tool and fails when any skill evals/ directory reaches a plan.

The source revision is provenance the harvester records; a harvested document is edited to plant its defect, so nothing in the tree can compare it with the revision, and the owner reads it at validation.

ACE-D2 makes the owner the acceptance authority on the one-defect property at validation, with the run report, decision and digests recorded; that is the human-judgment rule satisfied, and no mechanical check can read defect count off two documents.
The validation record holds the run report, the owner decision and the digests; the case check refuses a case lacking any of them.
Same record for a control-only case, whose validation is one panel run.
ACE-D2: the owner confirms at validation that the planted defect is the one ACE-D3 names; the decision is part of the record the case check reads.
The dispatch record carries the isolation ACE-D6 fixes (fresh context, empty directory, no tools); the scorer refuses a run whose isolation differs.
Same.

A substituted transport is refused by ACE-A18 and a dispatch with no report leaves the case pending under ACE-A19; the evaluation stays incomplete until the transport returns, which is what waiting means in a tree nothing runs continuously.
A case whose site is none counts a detection only on a judge match.
Passes at four or five of five.
Holds at four or five of five.
P1 locks at four or five passing panel runs of five.
A pending run counts in no rate.

The judge identity the record can hold is its resolved model ID and prompt digest, and ACE-A20 refuses a mismatch with the calibration; the invocation path is not observable in a committed record and changes no judgment.
The calibration record names its labeller; a labeller other than the owner refuses the task.
A calibration record sharing an item with a failed calibration of an earlier prompt digest is refused.
A case-task calibration holding no mechanical detection is refused.
ACE-D8 states that writing the plan before dispatch rests on the operator; a committed tree holds no ordering evidence, and ACE-A53 holds what it can, that the reports match the plan.
A response ID is read from the transport response the report carries; the tree cannot ask the transport whether it issued it, so the record is an attestation like the committed reports themselves.
ACE-D8 states that committing every attempt rests on the operator; nothing in the tree sees a run nobody commits.
One attempt per fingerprint, locked, failed or retested.
A judge model change rescores stored reports with no lens dispatch.
The comparison refuses lock sets covering different cases.
The emitter suite reproduces the report from the committed lock sets the entry names.
The verification child is a tracker item the human closes under ACQ-D2; the tree cannot observe the tracker, and the slice list states the child stays open until every case holds a current lock.
The report names every case not locked with its failing or pending side.
Every check run twice over unchanged inputs answers the same way and writes nothing.
Same.

The gate clause in a continuation line is the delivery contract verification gate the work facade requires in that line, not a criterion of this spec; each slice obligations are the ACE criteria the same line lists.
Same as obligation-reduction-31.
Same as obligation-reduction-31.
Same as obligation-reduction-31.
One attempt per fingerprint, with the retest where one is earned; ACE-D8 reworded to match.
Usable reports match planned runs one to one; superseded repeat reports stay committed and match nothing.
Calibration record names the judge model ID; mismatch refused.
A locked fingerprint is refused a further attempt.
A lens with no control run behind a current lock fails ACQ-A27.

criteria: Continuation S2.5: the committed catalogue passes the case check
Continuation S2.6: a committed baseline attempt on every case
Continuation S2.6: a lens-level comparison per revised lens

parts.statement: The specified files and suites are delivered at their promised locations.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'The manifest evals/cases.json'; 'The directory evals/cases/<id>/ holds defective.md and control.md.' Ordered slices: 'evals/check_cases.py with its suite'; 'evals/plan_run.py, evals/score.py and evals/judge.md, their suites'; 'A comparison mode in evals/score.py and the registry test.'
obligations.statement: Deliver the evaluation documents, manifest, named helpers, judge prompt and suites in the specified evaluation tree.

parts.statement: Deployment excludes the evaluation cases.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'Cases live in src/user/.claude/skills/ac-attack/evals/, so they never deploy.'
obligations.statement: Evaluation cases never deploy.

parts.statement: Required manifest fields are present, and table-governed metadata matches the catalogue.
A harvested document's recorded source revision identifies its actual source.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'The manifest evals/cases.json gives each case' its ID, served parents, rule, lens, defect site, detection statement and 'the source revision of any harvested document.'
obligations.statement: The manifest supplies the prescribed case identity, ownership, expectation and provenance fields.

parts.statement: Pair documents exist, are nonidentical and differ in one contiguous hunk; control-only cases omit the defective document and site.
The pair actually contains exactly its stated defect, and the control corrects that defect.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'The control is the defective document with its one defect corrected, and the two differ in one contiguous hunk. A control-only case has no defective document and no site.'
obligations.statement: Each pair contains one defect and its correction, with one contiguous changed hunk; control-only cases have no defective document or site.

parts.statement: A pair receives the control lens run, owner review and required amendment before evaluation runs count.
A control-only case receives one validation panel run that the owner reads whole.
The checker refuses documents differing from recorded validation digests.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'the owner validates a case before its runs count'; the lens runs once over the control, the owner reads relevant objections, upheld objections require amendment; 'The manifest records the digests of the validated pair'; 'A control-only case is validated by one panel run, read whole.'
obligations.statement: Cases undergo the prescribed owner validation before their runs count, and validated document identity is enforced.

discharged_by: Continuation S2.5: the committed catalogue passes the case check
parts.statement: The catalogue includes the listed cases and rules, with the prescribed parents, rule, lens and child metadata, and each lens enforces its case's rule.
Case content represents the parent's Given defect and includes its no-finding clause in the prescribed place.

obligations.source: ACE-D3: 'A parent criterion's Given clause is its case's defect'; its no-finding clause is the correction or a feature in both documents outside the hunk; 'A case's lens is the owner ARO-D1 gives its rule.' ACE-D3's catalogue table.
obligations.statement: The catalogue follows the parent's cases and no-finding clauses, covers the standard's rules and uses their owning lenses.

parts.statement: C1 holds a current lock.
C2 holds a current lock.
C3 holds a current lock.
C4 holds a current lock.
C5 holds a current lock.
C6 holds a current lock.
C7 holds a current lock.
C8 holds a current lock.
C9 holds a current lock.
C10 holds a current lock.
C11 holds a current lock.
C12 holds a current lock.
C13 holds a current lock.
C14 holds a current lock.
C15 holds a current lock.
C16 holds a current lock.
C17 holds a current lock.
C18 through C27 and C29 each hold a current lock over the committed, accepted catalogue.
C28 holds a current lock.
P1 holds a current lock.

obligations.source: ACE-D3's catalogue and Child column. Ordered slice S2.7: 'It stays open until every case holds a current lock.' ACE-D8: 'The evaluation of record is the set of current locks.'
obligations.statement: The specified catalogue cases hold current locks in the evaluation of record.

parts.statement: Substituted models, efforts, transports and planned counts are refused; served model identity comes from response metadata.
Every run is a fresh dispatch without inherited evaluation conversation.
Codex reads only its prompt from an empty directory, and OpenRouter reads only its prompt with no tools.
Transport unavailability leaves the evaluation waiting for that transport.

obligations.source: ACE-D4: 'A run is one fresh dispatch of one lens over one document.' ACE-D6's configuration table; 'every lens reads only its prompt'; 'A run on a substituted model or effort does not count. A down transport means the evaluation waits.'
obligations.statement: Evaluation uses fresh, isolated dispatches of the production configuration and waits when its transport is unavailable.

parts.statement: For ordinary sites, detections use the mechanical match or the prescribed partial-citation judgment, and count no other objection.
Every absence-site detection requires a matching judge ruling, including a rule-and-none citation.
Control non-silence requires a matching judgment on an objection citing the rule or site.
Empty control reports supply the emptiness observations used for ACQ-A27.

obligations.source: ACE-D4: rule-and-site citations detect mechanically; rule-only or site-only citations require a matching judgment; 'A case whose site is none always goes to the judge'; controls are not silent only for matching eligible objections; 'A control run is empty when the lens reports empty.'
obligations.statement: Detection, silence and emptiness follow the specified objection-routing rules.

parts.statement: A panel run passes only when none of its four runs has a judged demand for implementation criteria.

obligations.source: ACE-D4: 'A P1 panel run is four runs, one per lens'; 'A panel run passes when all four of its runs pass.'
obligations.statement: P1 panel-run scoring considers all four lenses and fails a panel when any lens wrongly demands implementation criteria.

parts.statement: Detection passes at 4/5 and 8/10 and fails at 2/5 and 7/10.
Detection passes at 5/5 and fails at the other permitted failing totals: 0/5, 1/5 and 3/10 through 6/10.
Control holds at 4/5 and 8/10 and fails at 2/5 and 7/10.
Control holds at 5/5 and fails at the other permitted failing totals: 0/5, 1/5 and 3/10 through 6/10.
Only a 3/5 side receives a retest, and all ten runs determine its retested result.
P1's observed evaluation-of-record aggregate satisfies its threshold and retest rule.
P1 aggregate scoring applies the specified thresholds to other permitted panel-outcome distributions.
In the checked scoring fixtures, locks require both sides to pass, parents require every serving case locked, planned thresholds govern, and rates are not averaged across cases.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: sides pass at four of five; three of five receives one five-run retest and passes at eight of ten; 'No run is discarded. A side below three fails'; P1 uses the same threshold and retest; parent passage requires every serving case locked; 'No rate is averaged across cases.'
obligations.statement: Case and P1 locking use the prescribed thresholds and retest rules without discarding runs or averaging cases.

parts.statement: No usable report after two repeats, or an unruled objection, produces pending and incomplete status.
Pending cases are not scored as misses.
No third repeat is planned.

obligations.source: ACE-D4: a missing or wholly malformed report 'is repeated at most twice'; an unusable or unruled report 'leaves its case pending and the evaluation incomplete'; 'A pending case is never scored as a miss.'
obligations.statement: Unusable or unresolved runs leave their cases pending and the evaluation incomplete, with bounded repeats and no miss score.

parts.statement: The emptiness threshold passes at 80 percent and fails below it.
Every lens meets that pooled threshold in the evaluation of record, including its P1 controls.
The pooled emptiness rate receives no side retest.
The report supplies pooled detection and silence rates over current-lock runs without using them to average case results.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: a lens passes ACQ-A27 at 'at least 80 percent of the control runs behind its cases' current locks, P1's included'; the pooled rate earns no retest; 'The scorer also reports each lens's pooled rates, which decide nothing.'
obligations.statement: ACQ-A27 uses pooled empty-control rates behind current locks, including P1, and the scorer reports pooled detection and silence rates.

parts.statement: Judgments use Claude Opus through the native Agent tool with evals/judge.md.
The assembled judge input contains exactly the permitted fields and excludes lens, model and arm identity.

obligations.source: ACE-D5: 'The judge is Claude Opus through the native Agent tool, with the prompt evals/judge.md'; case input is rule text, detection statement and one objection; P1 input is one objection; 'It never sees the lens, the model or the arm.'
obligations.statement: The prescribed judge receives only its allowed case or P1 input and cannot see lens, model or arm identity.

parts.statement: The scorer rejects calibration records below 18/20, with a mismatching prompt digest or without a resolved judge model ID.
Scott Hamilton actually labels the twenty task-specific calibration items.
A prompt revised after failed calibration uses twenty new calibration items.
Case-task calibration includes mechanical detections.
Compared lock sets share the resolved judge model ID and prompt digest.

obligations.source: ACE-D5: Scott Hamilton 'labels twenty items for the task, and the judge must agree on eighteen'; a revised prompt uses 'twenty new items'; case-task items 'include mechanical detections'; experiment tasks are calibrated the same way; comparison requires one judge model ID and prompt digest.
obligations.statement: Judgment tasks count only after the specified owner calibration, with renewed samples after failed revisions and compatible judge identity.

parts.statement: The complete plan is fixed before any dispatch.
Scoring uses response model metadata, requires one-to-one plan correspondence and rejects duplicate response IDs.
Every report includes its actual transport-provided response ID.

discharged_by: Continuation S2.6: a committed baseline attempt on every case
parts.statement: The baseline attempt on every catalogue case is committed.
Every other attempt and all its reports are committed at the prescribed run location, including failures and final attempts.
A new attempt is refused while a planned attempt has no committed reports, and after an unchanged fingerprint has an attempt and retest.
A below-three failure cannot obtain another unchanged-fingerprint attempt merely because it received no retest.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: 'The planner writes an attempt's plan before any dispatch'; it fixes dispatches, configuration, thresholds and cases; 'Every attempt is committed with its reports under evals/runs/<run-id>/, whatever it shows'; reports carry the transport's model and response ID; reports match plans one to one; exhausted fingerprints are refused; 'A failed case is then answered only by changing something.'
obligations.statement: Attempts are planned before dispatch, have authentic response metadata and complete committed reports, and cannot bypass the fingerprint's attempt budget.

parts.statement: Changed documents or emitted prompts void exactly affected fingerprinted locks, and evaluation-of-record cases have current locks.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: fingerprints contain emitted-prompt digests and ACE-D6 model and effort; emitted prompts contain lens body, shared template and enforced rules; 'P1's fingerprint covers all four lenses'; 'A change voids only the locks whose fingerprint it alters.'
obligations.statement: Current locks are tied to emitted document prompts and production configuration, with P1 covering all lenses and changes voiding only affected locks.

parts.statement: Judge-prompt and scorer changes rescore stored reports without lens dispatch, retaining only passing locks.
A judge-model-only change follows the same rescore and no-dispatch rule.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: 'A change to the judge prompt, the judge model or the scorer dispatches no lens. The stored reports are rescored, and a lock stands when its case still passes.'
obligations.statement: Judge and scorer changes rescore stored reports without dispatching lenses, retaining only passing locks.

parts.statement: A plan over 310 dispatches without named owner approval is refused with its count.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: 'Locking the whole catalogue from nothing plans 310 lens dispatches'; 'The planner refuses a larger plan, an experiment's included, unless the plan names the owner's approval.'
obligations.statement: Plans exceeding the approved dispatch budget require named owner approval.

parts.statement: Same-case fixture comparisons report improves exactly for preserved baseline locks and gains in at least two lenses; otherwise they name regression or missing gain.
Different case populations cannot create an unsupported improvement; disjoint populations produce no gain and name the missing gain.
Comparison refuses incompatible production configuration, judge identity or pending cases.

obligations.source: ACE-D9: improvement is 'over the same cases'; every baseline lock is preserved and at least two lenses gain a lock. ACE-D5 requires matching judge identity. What-if text: 'Lock sets sharing no case gain nothing, so the comparison names the missing gain.'
obligations.statement: Comparison applies the defined improvement rule over comparable case populations and refuses incompatible or pending evidence.

parts.statement: The emitter suite rejects a missing qualifying registry report and an incorrect current-template baseline digest.
The qualifying report is supported by actual whole-catalogue evidence from the template without the addition and demonstrates the defined improvement.

obligations.source: ACE-D9: 'An addition to the shared attack template ships only with a whole-catalogue comparison reporting improves against the template without it'; improvement preserves baseline locks and gains locks in two lenses; 'A test pins the template's digest to a registry of comparison reports.'
obligations.statement: Shared-template additions ship only with whole-catalogue evidence of the defined improvement against the template without the addition.

discharged_by: Continuation S2.6: a committed baseline attempt on every case
parts.statement: A baseline attempt exists on every case.

discharged_by: Continuation S2.6: a lens-level comparison per revised lens
parts.statement: Each revised lens has a lens-level comparison artifact.
The final revised lenses regress no catalogue case, because every catalogue case holds a current lock.

obligations.source: Ordered slice S2.6: 'A baseline attempt on every case, then body revisions for the rules each lens gained, each shown by a lens-level comparison to regress no case.'
obligations.statement: Lens revision work starts from a baseline on every case and supplies a lens-level comparison showing no regression.

parts.statement: The child cannot close while any required case lacks a current lock.

obligations.source: Ordered slice S2.7: 'The verification child for every review-outcome criterion'; 'It stays open until every case holds a current lock.'
obligations.statement: The evaluation verification child remains open until all cases have current locks.

parts.statement: A failed case is named in the evaluation failure result.

obligations.source: What-if text for ACE-A25 to ACE-A45: 'A failure names the failing case.'
obligations.statement: Evaluation failures identify the failing case.

parts.statement: A check does not mutate its input or persistent evaluation state.
Repeating a check over unchanged inputs yields the same answer.

obligations.source: What-if text: 'Every check is a read, so running it twice or with nothing changed answers the same way.'
obligations.statement: Checks are reads and answer consistently when repeated without changes.

ground.reason: ACE-D9 promises that a shared-template addition ships only with a whole-catalogue comparison reporting improves against the template without it. ACE-A24 exempts the baseline entry from that check and requires its digest to equal the current template. Making the addition the current baseline therefore passes without establishing the promised improvement.

objections.objection: A template addition can pass the emitter gate without any comparison evidence.

scenario.expect: The check passes while the addition has no whole-catalogue comparison reporting improves against the template without it.
scenario.given: A shared-template addition whose digest is recorded as the registry's baseline entry, with no comparison report for the addition.
scenario.when: The emitter suite applies ACE-A24's baseline exception and current-template digest check.

ground.reason: ACE-D5 says a judgment task counts only after calibration and requires the judge to agree with eighteen owner labels. ACE-A20 checks agreement count, prompt-digest equality and the presence of a resolved judge model ID. It does not require the calibrated model ID to match the model performing the judgment. ACE-D8 explicitly permits judge-model changes.

objections.objection: A replacement judge model can score judgments using another model's calibration.

scenario.expect: The checks pass while model B has never demonstrated the required calibration agreement.
scenario.given: A calibration record showing eighteen agreements under resolved judge model A, followed by judgments under resolved model B using the same prompt digest. Both model IDs are recorded.
scenario.when: The scorer applies ACE-A20's calibration checks.

ground.reason: ACE-D3 assigns C18–C27 and C29 distinct expectations, including decision-document assessment, human measurement, observation windows and several what-if questions. ACE-A42 combines all eleven case outcomes and catalogue acceptance into one criterion. These outcomes can be delivered and accepted independently.

objections.objection: ACE-A42 makes independently deliverable rule outcomes share one acceptance decision.

scenario.expect: The combined criterion passes, but it provides no separate criterion-level acceptance decision for the decision-document, human-measurement or observation-window obligations.
scenario.given: An accepted committed catalogue with current locks for C18–C27 and C29.
scenario.when: The scorer checks ACE-A42.

ground.reason: The checks observe catalogue contents and scorer behaviour, but do not establish the promised file layout or delivery of the named helpers and suites.

objections.objection: The implementation can provide the checked behaviour while omitting the specified deliverable files.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but evals/plan_run.py and the promised standalone suites are absent.
scenario.given: Equivalent callable helpers provide all checked behaviour, and the gate exits successfully.
scenario.when: The criteria are checked.

ground.reason: No criterion observes deployment output.

objections.objection: Evaluation cases can deploy despite the promise that they never deploy.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but evaluation documents appear in the deployed skill.
scenario.given: The catalogue and evaluation machinery satisfy all checks, while deployment includes evals/.
scenario.when: The skill is deployed.

ground.reason: Checking that a source-revision field exists does not check that it identifies the harvested source.

objections.objection: A harvested case can carry an unrelated source revision.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the manifest attributes the case to a revision that did not supply its document.
scenario.given: A valid harvested case has all required fields, correct validation digests and an incorrect source revision.
scenario.when: The catalogue check and evaluation run.

ground.reason: One contiguous hunk and matching validation digests establish document shape and identity, not a single corrected defect.

objections.objection: A pair can contain an additional defect or fail to correct its stated defect.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the pair contains an unrelated second defect.
scenario.given: The documents differ in one hunk, their recorded digests match, and the additional defect does not affect the scored detection statement.
scenario.when: The pair is checked and its runs are scored.

ground.reason: No criterion checks that the owner performed the required control review before runs counted.

objections.objection: A pair can be treated as validated without the prescribed owner review and correction process.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the owner never reads the relevant control objections.
scenario.given: Validation digests are recorded without owner review, and subsequent scored runs meet every threshold.
scenario.when: The case is accepted and locked.

ground.reason: Passing P1's scored panel runs does not establish that its preliminary validation panel was read whole by the owner.

objections.objection: A control-only case can enter evaluation without its required whole-panel validation.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but no owner reads a complete P1 validation panel.
scenario.given: P1 has accepted metadata and passing evaluation runs, but its validation record was created without the prescribed review.
scenario.when: P1 receives a current lock.

ground.reason: The metadata checks and lock checks do not compare case content with the parent's Given and no-finding clauses.

objections.objection: A case can serve the listed parent in metadata while testing a different defect or omitting its no-finding feature.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but C1 does not represent ACQ-A1's Given clause.
scenario.given: C1 has the required metadata and a valid single-defect pair that the lens reliably detects, but the defect differs from the parent's stated case.
scenario.when: The catalogue is checked and C1 is locked.

ground.reason: Distinct response IDs and matching configuration do not establish a fresh dispatch context.

objections.objection: Runs can reuse a conversation containing earlier documents or objections.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but later runs inherit earlier evaluation context.
scenario.given: A dispatcher reuses sessions while producing distinct response IDs and the required model, effort and run counts.
scenario.when: Five runs are collected for each document.

ground.reason: ACE-A18 checks configuration fields, not the empty-directory and no-tools restrictions.

objections.objection: A correctly identified production model can read the repository or use tools.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but a lens can read the case catalogue.
scenario.given: Models, effort, transport and counts match, while Codex runs in the repository or OpenRouter receives tools.
scenario.when: The evaluation dispatches its lenses.

ground.reason: Refusing substituted configurations and marking unusable reports pending do not require waiting for an unavailable transport.

objections.objection: A transport outage can terminate the evaluation instead of leaving it waiting.

scenario.expect: Every acceptance check passes, but the outage path terminates the evaluation permanently.
scenario.given: The normal evaluation and fixtures pass, while the dispatcher treats an unavailable transport as a terminal error.
scenario.when: The required transport becomes unavailable.

ground.reason: The detection criterion does not explicitly test the exception that an absence site always requires judgment.

objections.objection: An objection with the correct rule and site none can be counted mechanically despite a negative judgment.

scenario.expect: Every specified fixture check and current-lock check passes, but this absence objection counts as a detection.
scenario.given: An absence-site report cites the case's rule and target none, and the judge says it does not describe the detection statement.
scenario.when: The scorer applies its rule-and-site shortcut.

ground.reason: The specified detection fixtures cover totals 4/5, 8/10, 7/10 and 2/5, leaving other permitted totals unpinned.

objections.objection: Detection scoring can reject 5/5 or accept an untested failing total.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but a case detecting five times in five fails its detection side.
scenario.given: The named fixtures and current locks use the specified passing and failing totals; the scorer mishandles 5/5.
scenario.when: A new permitted attempt produces five detections.

ground.reason: The specified control fixtures cover totals 4/5, 8/10, 7/10 and 2/5, leaving other permitted totals unpinned.

objections.objection: Control scoring can reject 5/5 or accept an untested failing total.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but a control silent five times in five fails its control side.
scenario.given: The named fixtures and current locks use the specified totals; the scorer mishandles 5/5 silence.
scenario.when: A new permitted attempt produces five silent control runs.

ground.reason: ACE-A51 checks individual panel runs, and ACE-A41 checks the observed P1 lock; neither requires aggregate fixtures covering P1's other permitted outcomes.

objections.objection: P1's aggregate threshold can work for the current record while failing another allowed distribution.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but P1 is rejected when all five panel runs pass.
scenario.given: The current P1 lock uses four passing panel runs, and individual panel scoring is correct, but aggregate scoring rejects five of five.
scenario.when: P1 is evaluated with five passing panels.

ground.reason: Reporting pending and incomplete does not check that unresolved runs are excluded from miss scoring.

objections.objection: The scorer can mark a case pending while also counting its unresolved run as a miss.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the unresolved run increments the miss count.
scenario.given: A fixture has no usable report after two repeats; the scorer correctly emits pending and incomplete.
scenario.when: The scorer also updates detection statistics.

ground.reason: Calibration metadata and comparison compatibility do not pin Claude Opus, the native Agent tool or the prescribed judge prompt file.

objections.objection: A different judge implementation can satisfy every check.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but judgments come from another model through another transport.
scenario.given: The replacement judge has a resolved ID, matching prompt digests and a passing calibration record.
scenario.when: The evaluation requests judgments.

ground.reason: A record showing eighteen agreements does not establish that Scott Hamilton supplied the twenty labels.

objections.objection: Calibration can use labels supplied by another model or evaluator.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the calibration has no labels from Scott Hamilton.
scenario.given: A calibration record shows eighteen agreements in twenty using labels generated by another model.
scenario.when: ACE-A20's record check runs.

ground.reason: The record check does not establish that a revised prompt was calibrated on twenty new items.

objections.objection: A judge prompt can be tuned to a failed calibration set and then accepted on that same set.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the successful recalibration reuses the failed sample.
scenario.given: A revised prompt reaches eighteen agreements on the original twenty items and records its new digest.
scenario.when: The scorer accepts the recalibration record.

ground.reason: The agreement threshold does not check the required inclusion of mechanical detections in the calibration sample.

objections.objection: Calibration can omit the items intended to test false mechanical detections.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but no mechanical detection appears in the case-task calibration.
scenario.given: Twenty non-mechanical items produce eighteen agreements and valid metadata.
scenario.when: The scorer accepts the calibration.

ground.reason: Matching reports to a plan and scoring under its thresholds do not establish that the plan existed before dispatch.

objections.objection: An operator can construct the plan after seeing the reports.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the plan was written after all dispatches.
scenario.given: Reports have valid configuration and unique response IDs, and a matching plan is subsequently written.
scenario.when: The scorer checks correspondence and produces locks.

ground.reason: Uniqueness and plan correspondence do not require each response ID to be present and taken from the transport's own metadata.

objections.objection: Reports can use invented response IDs instead of the transport's IDs.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but recorded response IDs do not identify the actual responses.
scenario.given: Reports retain genuine model metadata but replace response IDs with distinct locally generated values.
scenario.when: The scorer checks report correspondence and duplicate IDs.

ground.reason: Blocking a subsequent attempt with no committed reports does not check that every completed attempt is committed in full.

objections.objection: A final failed attempt can remain uncommitted.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the last attempt and its reports are absent from git.
scenario.given: All required baseline attempts and current locks are committed, followed by an additional failed attempt that is not committed.
scenario.when: No subsequent attempt is requested.

ground.reason: ACE-A21 refuses another attempt only after an attempt and its retest; ACE-A46 forbids a retest below three of five.

objections.objection: A case failing below three of five can receive another attempt without a fingerprint change.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the planner permits another attempt on the unchanged failed case.
scenario.given: The first attempt detects twice in five, its reports are committed, and no retest is allowed.
scenario.when: A second attempt is requested on the same fingerprint.

ground.reason: ACE-A48 covers changes to the judge prompt or scorer, but not a judge-model-only change.

objections.objection: A judge model change can leave locks unrescored or trigger new lens dispatches.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but stored reports are not rescored when only the judge model changes.
scenario.given: Prompt-change and scorer-change fixtures pass; the judge-model-only path retains existing locks unchanged.
scenario.when: The resolved judge model changes.

ground.reason: ACE-A22 checks lock sets over the same cases, and ACE-A23 does not check differing case populations.

objections.objection: A comparison can report improvement for lock sets sharing no case.

scenario.expect: Every specified comparison check passes, but the disjoint comparison reports improves.
scenario.given: Two lock sets have matching configuration and judge identity, no pending cases and disjoint case populations.
scenario.when: The comparison counts new locks in two lenses as gains.

ground.reason: A registry report saying improves does not establish that its evidence actually comes from the template without the addition and demonstrates the defined gains.

objections.objection: A template addition can pass the registry gate using an unsupported comparison claim.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the actual baseline has no two-lens gain under the addition.
scenario.given: Comparison fixtures are correct and the current catalogue is locked, while the registry contains a report claiming improves using unsupported baseline evidence.
scenario.when: The emitter suite checks the digest and the report's declared result.

ground.reason: Current-lock checks do not observe whether the verification child remained open before those locks existed.

objections.objection: The verification child can close before the evaluation is complete.

scenario.expect: Every criterion eventually passes, but the verification child closed while cases lacked current locks.
scenario.given: The implementation closes the child early and later completes all required evaluation runs.
scenario.when: The final criteria are checked.

ground.reason: The scoring criteria check pass/fail results without requiring a failing-case identifier in the evaluation failure report.

objections.objection: An evaluation failure can be reported without naming its failing case.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the failing fixture produces only an anonymous failure result.
scenario.given: Threshold fixtures fail correctly, and the current evaluation is locked, but failure output omits case IDs.
scenario.when: A case fails its evaluation.

ground.reason: No criterion observes state preservation across a check.

objections.objection: Checks can mutate evaluation state despite the statement that every check is a read.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but a check updates a persistent evaluation counter.
scenario.given: The check returns every required result while writing additional state.
scenario.when: The check runs.

ground.reason: No criterion requires a second check on unchanged input to return the same answer.

objections.objection: A check can change its answer when repeated without an input change.

scenario.expect: Every first-run criterion check passes, but repeating the public check changes its answer.
scenario.given: Fresh fixture setups pass, while the checker retains invocation-dependent state.
scenario.when: The same check runs again over unchanged documents and reports.

ground.reason: ACE-A21 and ACE-D8 refuse a new attempt only once a fingerprint 'has had its attempt and its retest', but ACE-D7 earns a retest only at exactly three of five; a side that fails below three gets no retest, so the refusal condition never becomes true even though ACE-D8 declares such a failed case 'answered only by changing something'.

objections.objection: A case that fails at two of five on a side earns no retest, and the criteria then both forbid a further attempt on the unchanged fingerprint (ACE-D8's 'answered only by changing something') and permit one (ACE-A21's refusal triggers only after an attempt AND its retest, and no retest exists).

scenario.expect: Under ACE-D8's 'a failed case is then answered only by changing something' the planner refuses; under ACE-A21's literal condition (attempt and its retest) it does not, since no retest was ever earned — the two criteria require incompatible verdicts in the same circumstance.
scenario.given: A case whose current fingerprint has one committed attempt in which its detection side scored two of five, below the retest threshold
scenario.when: the planner is asked to plan a fresh attempt on the same unchanged fingerprint

ground.reason: ACE-D4 allows a run to be repeated at most twice and ACE-A18 says repeats do not count against the planned run count, while ACE-A53 requires the attempt's reports to match its plan one to one; the criteria never state whether repeated-run reports participate in the one-to-one matching.

objections.objection: The wording leaves open how the scorer matches reports to a plan when a run was repeated: one reading matches only the final usable report per planned run and accepts the attempt; another reads 'reports' as every committed report under evals/runs/<run-id>/ and refuses the attempt for holding more reports than planned runs.

scenario.expect: One reading scores the attempt normally (repeats exempt per ACE-A18); the other refuses it because six committed reports face five planned runs, so the same attempt is accepted or refused depending on which reading is taken.
scenario.given: A planned attempt of five runs per document in which one run's first report was malformed and ACE-D4's repeat produced a second, usable report, with both reports committed under the run directory as ACE-D8 requires
scenario.when: the scorer checks the attempt's reports against its plan under ACE-A53

ground.reason: ACE-A20 refuses a judgment task whose calibration record names a different prompt digest or lacks a resolved judge model ID, but nothing requires the calibration to have been performed under the same judge model ID as the run. ACE-D5 calibrates a prompt, and ACE-A23 locks comparisons to one judge model ID, yet scoring itself never checks that the calibration measured the judge that is actually ruling.

objections.objection: A calibration earned under one resolved judge model is accepted as calibrating a different judge model running the same prompt, so every judgment in the run rests on an evaluator that was never calibrated.

scenario.expect: the scorer refuses the judgment task, naming the judge model mismatch, which no criterion checks
scenario.given: a calibration record showing eighteen agreements in twenty, recorded under judge model ID X and prompt digest D
scenario.when: the scorer scores a run whose judge resolved to model ID Y with the same prompt digest D

ground.reason: ACE-A21 refuses a new attempt only on a fingerprint that has had its attempt and its retest, but a side that passed at four or five of five never earns a retest, so the refusal never triggers for an already-locked case. Re-running a passed case spends the dispatch budget ACE-D7 caps and, under ACE-D8's every-run-counts rule, can only un-lock or duplicate a standing lock; the document neither covers nor rules this out.

objections.objection: The planner allows a redundant attempt on a case whose unchanged fingerprint already holds a lock, letting a lucky-fail re-run destabilize the evaluation of record with no gain in evidence.

scenario.expect: the planner refuses, naming the case's existing current lock, which no criterion checks
scenario.given: a case holding a current lock from an attempt that passed both sides with no retest, and a tree whose fingerprint for that case is unchanged
scenario.when: the planner is asked to plan a new attempt on that case

ground.reason: ACE-A17 fixes the ACQ-A27 verdict at 80 percent of the control runs behind a lens's current locks, but a lens whose cases all failed holds no locks and contributes zero control runs, leaving the pooled rate undefined at the empty limit. ACE-A43 requires every lens to pass, so the scorer must still emit a verdict or a report entry (ACE-A49) for that lens, and no criterion says what either holds.

objections.objection: The scorer's behavior on an empty pool is unspecified: it may pass vacuously, crash, or omit the lens, and any of those silently corrupts the ACQ-A43 verdict and the pooled-rate report.

scenario.expect: a defined outcome, such as failing the lens for lack of evidence, which no criterion checks
scenario.given: a lens whose cases hold no current locks, so zero control runs stand behind them
scenario.when: the scorer computes the lens's pooled empty-control rate for ACQ-A27
